messages:
alex: Quick check — we're seeing an extra User-Agent header showing up on streaming connections from the rust-sdk. Any ideas?

maria: I noticed that too earlier today. The rust lib sets a default UA like `redwood-rust/0.1.0 (tokio/1.x)`. It should only be one header unless something upstream also sets it.

alex: Reproduced with a minimal app. Looks like UA gets injected by the HTTP client and again by our SDK wrapper. snippet where it happens: 
```rust
let ua = format!("redwood-rust/{}", VERSION);
req.headers.insert("user-agent", HeaderValue::from_str(&ua)?);
client.send(req).await?;
```

ryan: small note: that `&format!()` won't compile as written but I get the idea :) In our code we also add an `X-Client-Metrics: enabled` header by default. For folks wanting to opt-out, the env var is `REDWOOD_CLIENT_METRICS=0`.

sophie: For trace propagation: we inject `traceparent` and sometimes `tracestate`. The SDK auto-propagates by default. To disable propagation you can set `REDWOOD_PROPAGATE_TRACES=false` or call the client option to turn it off.

maria: Another streaming gotcha — retries. Streaming requests use an `x-rw-stream-id` header to correlate sessions. If you retry a stream but don't preserve the cache/kv cursor on the server side, you end up with duplicate partial sessions (ghost sessions).

alex: Good to know. Is there an open issue or PR for the UA duplication? I'm about to ping a reviewer. @ryan can you take a look at the small fix I made that avoids setting UA if the header already exists?

ryan: On it. I'll add a unit test to ensure we don't double-set headers and also a streaming integration test to validate `x-rw-stream-id` behavior across retries. I'll push a branch this afternoon.

devex-bot: deploy scheduled: 2026-03-20 03:00 UTC — staging -> canary 

sophie: Also a doc note: Java users sometimes see duplicates because `HttpRequest.Builder.header("User-Agent", ...)` can be called both by them and the SDK. Recommend calling `headers().setIfAbsent()` semantics in examples.

alex: Can someone add a short snippet in the devex quickstart explaining process-level vs per-client opt-out for metrics? I can file the doc PR but need the code examples.

maria: I added a draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/456 — includes env var and per-client examples for Python + Rust.

alex: Perfect. One last question: for self-hosted deployments, is the canonical recommendation `REDWOOD_CLIENT_METRICS=0` or prefer passing `client.with_metrics(false)`?

ryan: We recommend both depending on scope: env var for process-wide/system-level disable (good for infra), and the per-client option for library consumers who want fine-grained control. Example Java usage: 
```java
RedwoodClient client = RedwoodClient.builder()
  .apiKey(System.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
  .disableMetrics(true)
  .build();
```

sophie: I'll update the devex quickstart page and add a brief troubleshooting section for UA duplication, trace propagation toggles, and stream-retry caveats. :white_check_mark:

alex: Awesome — thanks everyone. I'll wait for @ryan's review then merge the tiny fix and land the doc change.
